claim: Intraflagellar transport (IFT) is a conserved process of cargo transport in cilia that is essential for development and homeostasis in organisms ranging from algae to vertebrates.
source: Intraflagellar transport (IFT) is a conserved process of cargo transport in cilia that is essential for development and homeostasis in organisms ranging from algae to vertebrates.
evidence: This is a general statement about IFT supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Variants in genes encoding subunits of the IFT-A and IFT-B protein complexes are a common cause of genetic diseases known as ciliopathies in humans.
source: In humans, variants in genes encoding subunits of the cargo-adapting IFT-A and IFT-B protein complexes are a common cause of genetic diseases known as ciliopathies.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations throughout the manuscript and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The study combined chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry and cryo-electron tomography with AlphaFold2-based prediction to model the architecture of the IFT-A complex.
source: Here, we combined chemical cross-linking mass spectrometry and cryo-electron tomography with AlphaFold2-based prediction of both protein structures and interaction interfaces to model the overall architecture of the monomeric six-subunit IFT-A complex, as well as its polymeric assembly within cilia.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Most motile cilia have a 9+2 microtubule axoneme arrangement.
source: Most motile cilia have a 9+2 microtubule axoneme arrangement (Luck, 1984) and are responsible for propelling the cells or adjacent fluid.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Luck, 1984.

claim: Primary cilia lack the central pair of microtubules and serve a key role in cellular sensory functions.
source: In contrast, primary cilia lack the central pair of microtubules and serve a key role in cellular sensory functions (Bloodgood, 2009; Garcia-Gonzalo and Reiter, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Bloodgood, 2009 and Garcia-Gonzalo and Reiter, 2012.

claim: Ciliary defects are linked to developmental diseases known as ciliopathies in humans.
source: In humans, ciliary defects are linked to a number of developmental diseases, broadly known as ciliopathies (Legendre et al., 2021; Reiter and Leroux, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Legendre et al., 2021 and Reiter and Leroux, 2017.

claim: IFT was first defined in the flagellated, unicellular green algae Chlamydomonas.
source: First defined in the flagellated, unicellular green algae Chlamydomonas (Kozminski et al., 1993), IFT comprises transport of proteins and protein complexes from the cell body to the tip of the cilia by kinesin motors (anterograde), followed by the movement of molecules back to the cell body by dynein motors (retrograde) (Lechtreck et al., 2017; Taschner and Lorentzen, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kozminski et al., 1993.

claim: IFT comprises anterograde transport by kinesin motors and retrograde transport by dynein motors.
source: First defined in the flagellated, unicellular green algae Chlamydomonas (Kozminski et al., 1993), IFT comprises transport of proteins and protein complexes from the cell body to the tip of the cilia by kinesin motors (anterograde), followed by the movement of molecules back to the cell body by dynein motors (retrograde) (Lechtreck et al., 2017; Taschner and Lorentzen, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lechtreck et al., 2017 and Taschner and Lorentzen, 2016.

claim: IFT has been shown to transport transmembrane proteins.
source: IFT has been shown to transport transmembrane proteins (Huang et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2005; Kobayashi et al., 2021; Wingfield et al., 2018), tubulins (Craft et al., 2015; Hao et al., 2011), and chaperones (Bhowmick et al., 2009), among other cargoes necessary for proper ciliary function, although some ciliary proteins also move by diffusion (Ye et al., 2013; Belzile et al., 2013; Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2005; Kobayashi et al., 2021; Wingfield et al., 2018.

claim: IFT has been shown to transport tubulins.
source: IFT has been shown to transport transmembrane proteins (Huang et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2005; Kobayashi et al., 2021; Wingfield et al., 2018), tubulins (Craft et al., 2015; Hao et al., 2011), and chaperones (Bhowmick et al., 2009), among other cargoes necessary for proper ciliary function, although some ciliary proteins also move by diffusion (Ye et al., 2013; Belzile et al., 2013; Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Craft et al., 2015 and Hao et al., 2011.

claim: IFT has been shown to transport chaperones.
source: IFT has been shown to transport transmembrane proteins (Huang et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2005; Kobayashi et al., 2021; Wingfield et al., 2018), tubulins (Craft et al., 2015; Hao et al., 2011), and chaperones (Bhowmick et al., 2009), among other cargoes necessary for proper ciliary function, although some ciliary proteins also move by diffusion (Ye et al., 2013; Belzile et al., 2013; Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bhowmick et al., 2009.

claim: Some ciliary proteins move by diffusion.
source: IFT has been shown to transport transmembrane proteins (Huang et al., 2007; Qin et al., 2005; Kobayashi et al., 2021; Wingfield et al., 2018), tubulins (Craft et al., 2015; Hao et al., 2011), and chaperones (Bhowmick et al., 2009), among other cargoes necessary for proper ciliary function, although some ciliary proteins also move by diffusion (Ye et al., 2013; Belzile et al., 2013; Harris et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Ye et al., 2013; Belzile et al., 2013; Harris et al., 2016.

claim: Ciliary assembly and regulation by IFT are strongly conserved across evolution from unicellular organisms to complex animals.
source: Much of our understanding of IFT continues to emerge from work with simple organisms such as Chlamydomonas, trypanosomes, and the model single-celled ciliate Tetrahymena, but crucially, ciliary assembly and regulation by IFT are strongly conserved across evolution, from unicellular organisms to complex animals (Ishikawa and Marshall, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ishikawa and Marshall, 2017.

claim: Variants in genes encoding IFT proteins are commonly linked to ciliopathies.
source: Due to the vital role of IFT in ciliogenesis and maintenance, variants in genes encoding IFT proteins are commonly linked to ciliopathies (Pigino, 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pigino, 2021.

claim: IFT is critical for primary cilia assembly in mice.
source: For example, IFT is critical for primary cilia assembly in mice, where assembly defects are linked to renal disorders, such as polycystic kidney disease (Pazour et al., 2000), and IFT-dependent defects in Hedgehog signal transduction produce neural tube and skeletal abnormalities (Huangfu et al., 2003; Haycraft et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pazour et al., 2000.

claim: IFT assembly defects in mice are linked to renal disorders such as polycystic kidney disease.
source: For example, IFT is critical for primary cilia assembly in mice, where assembly defects are linked to renal disorders, such as polycystic kidney disease (Pazour et al., 2000), and IFT-dependent defects in Hedgehog signal transduction produce neural tube and skeletal abnormalities (Huangfu et al., 2003; Haycraft et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pazour et al., 2000.

claim: IFT-dependent defects in Hedgehog signal transduction produce neural tube and skeletal abnormalities in mice.
source: For example, IFT is critical for primary cilia assembly in mice, where assembly defects are linked to renal disorders, such as polycystic kidney disease (Pazour et al., 2000), and IFT-dependent defects in Hedgehog signal transduction produce neural tube and skeletal abnormalities (Huangfu et al., 2003; Haycraft et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Huangfu et al., 2003 and Haycraft et al., 2007.

claim: Variants in human genes encoding IFT components are associated with skeletal ciliopathies including Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy, cranioectodermal dysplasia, and short-rib polydactyly.
source: Likewise, in clinical studies, variants in human genes encoding IFT components are associated with several skeletal ciliopathies, including Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy, cranioectodermal dysplasia, and short-rib polydactyly (Gilissen et al., 2010; Ashe et al., 2012; Schmidts et al., 2013b; Taylor et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Gilissen et al., 2010; Ashe et al., 2012; Schmidts et al., 2013b; Taylor et al., 2015.

claim: Variants within a single IFT-A gene can be associated with multiple distinct ciliopathies.
source: Curiously, variants within a single IFT-A gene can be associated with multiple distinct ciliopathies (Davis et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Davis et al., 2011.

claim: The IFT complex consists of a six-subunit IFT-A complex and a larger 16-subunit IFT-B complex.
source: The IFT complex consists of two distinct subcomplexes, the six-subunit IFT-A complex and the larger, 16-subunit IFT-B (Taschner and Lorentzen, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Taschner and Lorentzen, 2016.

claim: Crystal structures have been determined for several IFT-B subunits.
source: While crystal structures have been determined for several IFT-B subunits (Taschner et al., 2016; Taschner et al., 2014; Bhogaraju et al., 2011; Wachter et al., 2019; Bhogaraju et al., 2013a; Taschner et al., 2018), no such structures exist for any IFT-A proteins.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Taschner et al., 2016; Taschner et al., 2014; Bhogaraju et al., 2011; Wachter et al., 2019; Bhogaraju et al., 2013a; Taschner et al., 2018.

claim: No crystal structures exist for any IFT-A proteins.
source: While crystal structures have been determined for several IFT-B subunits (Taschner et al., 2016; Taschner et al., 2014; Bhogaraju et al., 2011; Wachter et al., 2019; Bhogaraju et al., 2013a; Taschner et al., 2018), no such structures exist for any IFT-A proteins.
evidence: This statement is explicitly stated in the text.

claim: Cryo-electron tomography has provided an in situ view of the assembly of IFT complexes into polymeric structures known as IFT trains at the ciliary base.
source: Recently, cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) has provided a valuable in situ view of the assembly of IFT complexes into polymeric structures, known as IFT trains, at the ciliary base, highlighting their stepwise association (Klena et al., 2021), and capturing snapshots of IFT trains moving along the axonemes (Jordan et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Klena et al., 2021 and Jordan et al., 2018.

claim: Cryo-ET studies have revealed low-resolution structures of the IFT-A and IFT-B complexes.
source: These cryo-ET studies have not only revealed the low-resolution structures of the IFT-A and IFT-B complexes, but also revealed their cellular context, the mode of IFT-A/IFT-B associations, and the stoichiometries between the complexes.
evidence: This statement is supported by references to cryo-ET studies mentioned in the text.

claim: Cryo-ET has not provided high-resolution structures necessary to understand the molecular assembly of individual IFT-A proteins.
source: However, this technique has not provided the high-resolution structures necessary to understand the molecular assembly of the individual IFT-A proteins into the overall IFT super-complex.
evidence: This statement is explicitly stated in the text.

claim: The IFT-A model is validated by comparison to experimental evidence across multiple organisms.
source: We validate the model by comparison to experimental evidence across multiple organisms, consistent with the deep structural conservation of the IFT-A complex (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement describes the validation approach used in the study and is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: The IFT-A complex is deeply structurally conserved.
source: We validate the model by comparison to experimental evidence across multiple organisms, consistent with the deep structural conservation of the IFT-A complex (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: Four IFT-A proteins (IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144) are predicted to share the same general architecture of two WD40 head domains and a TPR tail domain.
source: Four of these proteins–IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144–are predicted to share the same general architecture of two Tryptophan/Aspartic Acid Repeat (WD40) head domains and a tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) tail domain, while IFT139 is composed of 19 TPR repeats, and the IFT43 domain structure is largely uncharacterized (Behal et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Behal et al., 2012.

claim: IFT139 is composed of 19 TPR repeats.
source: Four of these proteins–IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144–are predicted to share the same general architecture of two Tryptophan/Aspartic Acid Repeat (WD40) head domains and a tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) tail domain, while IFT139 is composed of 19 TPR repeats, and the IFT43 domain structure is largely uncharacterized (Behal et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Behal et al., 2012.

claim: The IFT43 domain structure is largely uncharacterized.
source: Four of these proteins–IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144–are predicted to share the same general architecture of two Tryptophan/Aspartic Acid Repeat (WD40) head domains and a tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR) tail domain, while IFT139 is composed of 19 TPR repeats, and the IFT43 domain structure is largely uncharacterized (Behal et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Behal et al., 2012.

claim: IFT-A proteins are broadly conserved across eukaryotes.
source: These proteins are broadly conserved across eukaryotes (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: AlphaFold2 predicted structures of full-length IFT-A proteins scored well by the predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT).
source: The computed models scored well by the predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT) (Tunyasuvunakool et al., 2021), with most of the residues falling within the confident prediction threshold (pLDDT >70).
evidence: This statement describes the quality of the AlphaFold2 predictions and is supported by a citation to Tunyasuvunakool et al., 2021.

claim: Most residues in the AlphaFold2 predicted IFT-A protein structures fall within the confident prediction threshold (pLDDT >70).
source: The computed models scored well by the predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT) (Tunyasuvunakool et al., 2021), with most of the residues falling within the confident prediction threshold (pLDDT >70).
evidence: This statement describes the quality of the AlphaFold2 predictions.

claim: DSSO covalently cross-links pairs of accessible lysine residues falling within a distance determined by the length of the DSSO linker itself and the linked lysine side chains.
source: DSSO covalently cross-links pairs of accessible lysine residues falling within a distance determined by the length of the DSSO linker itself and the linked lysine side chains (Merkley et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Merkley et al., 2014.

claim: The maximum distance for DSSO cross-links is generally less than 30 Å.
source: This is generally less than 30 Å, although we include an additional 5 Å margin of error to account for protein dynamics as in Erzberger et al., 2014; Fernandez-Martinez et al., 2016; LoPiccolo et al., 2015; Shi et al., 2014.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Erzberger et al., 2014; Fernandez-Martinez et al., 2016; LoPiccolo et al., 2015; Shi et al., 2014.

claim: A total of 69 intramolecular cross-links were identified between amino acids spanning the length of each individual IFT-A protein, apart from IFT43.
source: We identified a total of 69 intramolecular cross-links between amino acids spanning the length of each individual IFT-A protein, apart from IFT43 (Figure 1B, purple arcs).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 97% of all cross-linked residue pairs fell within the 35 Å length restraint in the Tetrahymena IFT-A protein models.
source: Our XL/MS data strongly validated the predicted structures, as 97% of all cross-linked residue pairs fell within the 35 Å length restraint in the models (Figure 1C, pink in violin plots).
evidence: This statement describes the concordance between experimental cross-linking data and AlphaFold2 predictions, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Intramolecular cross-linked residues separated by more than 500 residues in their primary sequence fell within 35 Å in the 3D structure.
source: Impressively, even intramolecular cross-linked residues separated by more than 500 residues in their primary sequence fell within 35 Å in the 3D structure (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This statement describes experimental data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: The structures of the IFT-A complex and its subunits are expected to be highly conserved across eukaryotes.
source: The structures of the IFT-A complex and its subunits are expected to be highly conserved across eukaryotes (van Dam et al., 2013), so we explored this relationship by superimposing models of IFT-A proteins from C. reinhardtii on those for T. thermophila.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: Tetrahymena-derived chemical cross-links were strongly in agreement with the C. reinhardtii structures, although the concordance was slightly weaker than with Tetrahymena structures.
source: As expected, our Tetrahymena-derived chemical cross-links were still strongly in agreement with the C. reinhardtii structures, although as expected the concordance was slightly weaker (Figure 1C, green).
evidence: This statement describes the comparison between Tetrahymena cross-links and C. reinhardtii structures, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 86% agreement was observed between the human IFT-A model and the Tetrahymena XL/MS data.
source: Accordingly, we observed 86% agreement between the human model and the Tetrahymena XL/MS data, measured as the percentage of XL/MS amino acid pairs that were predicted to be 35 Å or less apart when mapped onto the AlphaFold2 models of human IFT proteins.
evidence: This statement describes the concordance between human models and Tetrahymena experimental data.

claim: Near-perfect concordance was found between AlphaFold-predicted interaction partners and experimentally confirmed interaction partners, with the sole exception being a high-confidence AlphaFold interaction between IFT122 and IFT139 with no supporting cross-links.
source: We found near-perfect concordance between AlphaFold-predicted interaction partners and the experimentally confirmed interaction partners, the sole exception being a high-confidence AlphaFold interaction between IFT122 and IFT139 with no supporting cross-links.
evidence: This statement describes the comparison between AlphaFold predictions and experimental cross-linking data.

claim: The top-scoring cluster of IFT-A models had a weighted root-mean-square (RMSF) cluster precision of 15 Å.
source: The cluster had a weighted root-mean-square (RMSF) cluster precision of 15 Å (Viswanath et al., 2017), which denotes the average fluctuations of the individual residues (or beads) in 3D space across the ensemble.
evidence: This statement describes a quantitative measure of the model quality and is supported by a citation to Viswanath et al., 2017.

claim: 92% of the cross-links were well-satisfied by the top-scoring ensemble of IFT-A models.
source: In all, 92% of the cross-links were well-satisfied by our top-scoring ensemble of models (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This statement describes the validation of the model against experimental cross-linking data, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: A high cross-correlation coefficient (.94) was observed between two halves of the final cluster, confirming a high degree of convergence.
source: We observed a high cross-correlation coefficient between the two samples (.94) confirming a high degree of convergence between models in our final cluster (Viswanath et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement describes a quantitative measure of model convergence and is supported by a citation to Viswanath et al., 2017.

claim: A 23 Å resolution structure of the IFT-A complex was determined by cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging.
source: To address these questions, we determined a 23 Å resolution structure of the IFT-A complex by cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging, as observed in situ in the context of a flagellar anterograde IFT transport train within intact Chlamydomonas flagella (Figure 3).
evidence: This statement describes the cryo-ET structure determination, shown in Figure 3.

claim: 7900 additional particles were incorporated into the subtomogram averaging from previous studies.
source: To arrive at this structure, we incorporated 7900 additional particles into the subtomogram averaging from our previous studies (Jordan et al., 2018; Jordan and Pigino, 2019; Table 1 and Methods), and this improved resolution served to constrain and inform our modeling.
evidence: This statement describes the data used for subtomogram averaging and is supported by citations to Jordan et al., 2018 and Jordan and Pigino, 2019.

claim: Rigidly docking the IFT-A monomer model placed 54% of the atoms within the subtomogram average map.
source: Rigidly docking the model placed 54% of the atoms within the map.
evidence: This statement describes the initial fit of the model into the cryo-ET density.

claim: IFT43, IFT121, IFT139, and the N-terminus of IFT122 fit better into the subtomogram average with 67% of the atoms within the map.
source: IFT43, IFT121, IFT139, and the C-terminus of IFT122 subcomplex fit better into the subtomogram average with 67% of the atoms within the map.
evidence: This statement describes the fit of specific IFT-A subunits into the cryo-ET density.

claim: The final flexibly fit structure places 71% of all atoms within the subtomogram average map.
source: The final flexibly fit structure places 71% of all atoms within the map.
evidence: This statement describes the final fit of the model into the cryo-ET density after flexible fitting.

claim: IFT140 was observed to bridge adjacent IFT-A complexes within the train, with the N-terminus of IFT140 interacting with the C-terminus of an adjacent IFT140 protein.
source: Notably, we observed IFT140 rearranged to bridge adjacent IFT-A complexes within the train, with the N-terminus of IFT140 interacting with the C-terminus of an adjacent IFT140 protein.
evidence: This statement describes a structural observation from the model docked into the cryo-ET density.

claim: Co-sedimentation assays and VIP experiments in Chlamydomonas and mammalian cells suggest that IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144 form a core complex within IFT-A.
source: Both co-sedimentation assays and visual immunoprecipitation (VIP) experiments in Chlamydomonas and mammalian cells (Behal et al., 2012; Hirano et al., 2017) suggest that IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144 form a core complex within IFT-A (Figure 5B.I and B.II).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Behal et al., 2012 and Hirano et al., 2017, and shown in Figure 5B.I and B.II.

claim: The C-terminal domain of IFT122 directly interacts with IFT140 and IFT144.
source: Within this core complex, the C-terminal domain of IFT122 directly interacts with IFT140 and IFT144 (Takahara et al., 2018), with a stable heterodimer being formed between IFT122 and IFT144, and specifically, residues 357–653 of IFT144 are required for the interaction with IFT122 (Hirano et al., 2017; Takahara et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Takahara et al., 2018, Hirano et al., 2017.

claim: A stable heterodimer is formed between IFT122 and IFT144.
source: Within this core complex, the C-terminal domain of IFT122 directly interacts with IFT140 and IFT144 (Takahara et al., 2018), with a stable heterodimer being formed between IFT122 and IFT144, and specifically, residues 357–653 of IFT144 are required for the interaction with IFT122 (Hirano et al., 2017; Takahara et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Takahara et al., 2018, Hirano et al., 2017.

claim: Residues 357–653 of IFT144 are required for the interaction with IFT122.
source: Within this core complex, the C-terminal domain of IFT122 directly interacts with IFT140 and IFT144 (Takahara et al., 2018), with a stable heterodimer being formed between IFT122 and IFT144, and specifically, residues 357–653 of IFT144 are required for the interaction with IFT122 (Hirano et al., 2017; Takahara et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hirano et al., 2017 and Takahara et al., 2018.

claim: VIP assays show the N-terminal domain of IFT122 interacts with IFT121 and IFT43.
source: Furthermore, visible immunoprecipitation (VIP) assays show the N-terminal domain of IFT122 interacts with IFT121 and IFT43 (Takahara et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Takahara et al., 2018.

claim: The IFT-A model agrees with previous findings about IFT-A protein interactions.
source: Our model of the IFT-A structure agrees perfectly with these previous findings (Figure 5B.III-5B.VI).
evidence: This statement describes the validation of the model against prior literature, shown in Figure 5B.III-5B.VI.

claim: VIP experiments observed robust binding of the IFT121 C-terminal fragment to all other subunits in the complex.
source: VIP experiments were used to observe the robust binding of both the IFT121 C-terminal fragment to all other subunits in the complex and the IFT121 fragment 545–800 to IFT122 (Fu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2016.

claim: The IFT121 fragment 545–800 binds to IFT122.
source: VIP experiments were used to observe the robust binding of both the IFT121 C-terminal fragment to all other subunits in the complex and the IFT121 fragment 545–800 to IFT122 (Fu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2016.

claim: The interaction between IFT121 and IFT43 was observed for C. reinhardtii proteins by yeast two-hybrid assay and recombinant bacterial co-expression.
source: Moreover, the interaction between IFT121 and IFT43 was observed for C. reinhardtii proteins by yeast two-hybrid assay and recombinant bacterial co-expression (Behal et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Behal et al., 2012.

claim: Bacterial co-expression assays demonstrated an interaction between IFT122 and IFT43.
source: In addition, bacterial co-expression assays demonstrated an interaction between IFT122 and IFT43 (Behal et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Behal et al., 2012.

claim: VIP assays in mammalian cells suggest that IFT43, IFT121, and IFT122 interact with IFT139.
source: One study in mammalian cells using the VIP assay suggests that IFT43, IFT121, and IFT122 interact with IFT139.
evidence: This statement describes experimental findings from VIP assays.

claim: IFT122 may be required for the interaction of IFT139 with IFT43 and IFT121.
source: The study implies that IFT122 may be required for the interaction of IFT139 with IFT43 and IFT121 (Hirano et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hirano et al., 2017.

claim: The IFT-A model suggests that the interaction between the peripheral subunits (IFT43, IFT121, and IFT139) is facilitated by IFT122.
source: Interestingly, while our data showed no direct cross-links between IFT122 and IFT139, our model suggests that the interaction between the peripheral subunits (IFT43, IFT121, and IFT139) is facilitated by IFT122 (Figure 5B.XI).
evidence: This statement describes an inference from the model, shown in Figure 5B.XI.

claim: IFT139 loss-of-function experiments suggest that IFT139 is the most distal subunit.
source: It has also been suggested from IFT139 loss-of-function experiments that IFT139 is the most distal subunit (Hirano et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hirano et al., 2017.

claim: The IFT-A model places IFT139 most distal to the core.
source: Consistent with these data, our model places IFT139 most distal to the core (Figure 5B.XII).
evidence: This statement describes a structural feature of the model, shown in Figure 5B.XII.

claim: IFT has proven to be highly conserved despite organisms diverging since the last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA).
source: We constructed our model using spatial information from organisms that have diverged since the last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA). Despite this, IFT has proven to be highly conserved (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: There is a 41% sequence identity shared between the IFT172 protein from human and T. brucei.
source: In one example, there is a 41% sequence identity shared between the IFT172 protein from human and T. brucei, an early branching supergroup (Excavata) of eukaryotes (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: IFT-B subtomogram averages collected from mammalian primary cilia and C. reinhardtii motile cilia display similar overall morphologies.
source: This structural conservation between species is also evident from IFT-B subtomogram averages collected from mammalian primary cilia and C. reinhardtii motile cilia (Kiesel et al., 2020), which display similar overall morphologies to the IFT-B monomers.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kiesel et al., 2020.

claim: Phylogenetic evidence suggests that the IFT complex is a sister structure to COPI and a member of the proto-coatomer family.
source: Phylogenetic evidence suggests that the IFT complex is a sister structure to COPI and a member of the proto-coatomer family (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: The αβ subunits of the COPI complex interact via their TPR tail domain.
source: The ɑβ subunits of the COPI complex interact via their TPR tail domain (van Dam et al., 2013; Lee and Goldberg, 2010), and we observed a similar binding mode in IFT-A, where the subunits IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144 interact via their TPR tail domains (Figure 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to van Dam et al., 2013 and Lee and Goldberg, 2010, and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In IFT-A, the subunits IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144 interact via their TPR tail domains.
source: The ɑβ subunits of the COPI complex interact via their TPR tail domain (van Dam et al., 2013; Lee and Goldberg, 2010), and we observed a similar binding mode in IFT-A, where the subunits IFT121, IFT122, IFT140, and IFT144 interact via their TPR tail domains (Figure 6).
evidence: This statement describes a structural observation from the model, shown in Figure 6.

claim: Phylogenetic analyses suggest that IFT-A and the BBSome likely evolved from a single IFT complex through subunit duplication.
source: Phylogenetic analyses also suggest that IFT-A and the BBSome likely evolved from a single IFT complex through subunit duplication (van Dam et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to van Dam et al., 2013.

claim: In the BBSome, the TPR protein BBS4 interacts with the β-propeller of BBS1.
source: In the BBSome, the TPR protein, BBS4, interacts with the β-propeller of BBS1 (Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2020.

claim: In the IFT-A model, there is an analogous interaction between the WD40 domain of IFT122 and TPR-based IFT139.
source: Similarly, in our model of IFT-A, there is an analogous interaction between the WD40 domain of IFT122 and TPR-based IFT139.
evidence: This statement describes a structural observation from the model.

claim: TPR domains play a role in stabilizing intracomplex interactions.
source: This is not surprising given the reported role of TPR domains in stabilizing intracomplex interactions (Grove et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Grove et al., 2008.

claim: In clathrin, the WD40 domains are known to selectively bind unique cargo peptides in vesicular transport.
source: In clathrin, another complex identified in our search, the WD40 domains are known to selectively bind unique cargo peptides in vesicular transport (ter Haar et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to ter Haar et al., 2000.

claim: A similar function to cargo binding was previously suggested for the WD40 domains in IFT-A and the BBSome.
source: A similar function to this was previously suggested for the WD40 domains in IFT-A and the BBSome (Bhogaraju et al., 2013b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Bhogaraju et al., 2013b.

claim: The WD40 domains in TPR-containing proteins may be specialized for participating in transient interactions such as the binding of cargo proteins.
source: We hypothesize that the WD40 domains in these TPR-containing proteins may be specialized for participating in transient interactions such as the binding of cargo proteins and that this role may prove useful for explaining the position of the domains towards the exterior of the complex as well as the range of phenotypes associated with IFT-based diseases.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their structural model and comparison to other complexes.

claim: 79% of known disease-associated variants in IFT-A are located within the WD40 regions.
source: While we observe some disease-associated variants occurring within the TPR domains, the large majority of known disease-associated variants (79%) (Hamosh et al., 2005; Landrum et al., 2014) are located within the WD40 regions (Figure 7).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hamosh et al., 2005 and Landrum et al., 2014, and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Variants located on the WD40 domains may act by disrupting the association of important cargo proteins rather than by disrupting overall IFT-A complex formation.
source: This suggests that the variants located on the WD40 domains act by disrupting the association of important cargo proteins rather than by disrupting overall IFT-A complex formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the location of disease variants in the structural model.

claim: WD-repeat domains provide large surface areas for potential binding, allowing these domains to simultaneously bind several distinct cargo proteins.
source: This idea is consistent with the proposal that the WD-repeat domains provide large surface areas for potential binding, allowing these domains to simultaneously bind several distinct cargo proteins (Li and Roberts, 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Li and Roberts, 2001.

claim: Expression of IFT140 lacking the N-terminal WD repeats is sufficient to disrupt ciliogenesis to some extent but fails to rescue the ciliary localization of GTPases, lipid-anchored proteins, and cell signaling proteins.
source: Expression of IFT140 lacking the N-terminal WD repeats is sufficient to disrupt ciliogenesis to some extent but fails to rescue the ciliary localization of GTPases, lipid-anchored proteins, and cell signaling proteins (Picariello et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Picariello et al., 2019.

claim: The WD40 domains of IFT140 play an important role in cargo transport.
source: This result suggests that the WD40 domains play an important role in cargo transport (Picariello et al., 2019) and is consistent with the position of the IFT140 TPR domain in the core of the IFT-A complex and the position of the WD40 domains on the surface of the complex (Figure 8A).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Picariello et al., 2019 and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Two disease-associated missense variants in the IFT140 WD40 domains (Y311C and E664K) localize normally to axonemes.
source: With this in mind, it is interesting that two disease-associated missense variants in the IFT140 WD40 domains (Y311C and E664K) (Schmidts et al., 2013a; Perrault et al., 2012; Figure 8B) were shown to localize normally to axonemes (Perrault et al., 2012), indicating their normal interaction with other IFT-A proteins.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Schmidts et al., 2013a and Perrault et al., 2012, and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The S939P variant of IFT140 lies near the interaction interface with both IFT122 and IFT144 and displays aberrant cellular localization.
source: By contrast, the S939P variant of IFT40 lies not just in the TPR domain but also near the interaction interface with both IFT122 and IFT144 (Figure 8D) and this variant displays an aberrant cellular localization (Hull et al., 2016), suggesting failure to assemble into a normal IFT-A complex.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hull et al., 2016 and shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Loss of IFT122 results in ciliogenesis defects.
source: Likewise, loss of IFT122 results in ciliogenesis defects (Takahara et al., 2018), but cilia can be rescued by the ciliopathy-associated variants such as the W7C and G513V alleles (Takahara et al., 2018), which do not map to the TPR domains but instead to the WD40 repeats (Figure 8C).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Takahara et al., 2018.

claim: Cilia can be rescued by the ciliopathy-associated IFT122 variants W7C and G513V.
source: Likewise, loss of IFT122 results in ciliogenesis defects (Takahara et al., 2018), but cilia can be rescued by the ciliopathy-associated variants such as the W7C and G513V alleles (Takahara et al., 2018), which do not map to the TPR domains but instead to the WD40 repeats (Figure 8C).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Takahara et al., 2018 and shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Cilia rescued with IFT122 disease-associated alleles W7C and G513V exhibit abnormal localization of the ciliary proteins INPP5E and GPR161.
source: Moreover, cilia rescued with these disease-associated alleles still exhibit abnormal localization of the ciliary proteins INPP5E and GPR161 (Takahara et al., 2018), raising the possibility that they specifically disrupt the association of IFT122 with membrane protein cargoes.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Takahara et al., 2018.

claim: Ciliopathy-associated missense variants in the WD40 domains of IFT122, including S373F and V553G, disrupt the association of the IFT-A core with the IFT-A peripheral proteins IFT121 and IFT43.
source: These and other ciliopathy-associated missense variants in the WD40 domains of IFT122, including S373F and V553G, also disrupt the association of the IFT-A core with the IFT-A peripheral proteins, IFT121 and IFT43 (Takahara et al., 2018), and the positions of all of these alleles near those interfaces in our model are consistent with this result (Figure 8C).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Takahara et al., 2018 and shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The L795P variant in IFT139 lies in the TPR domain near the protein's interface with IFT121.
source: The L795P variant in the peripheral component IFT139 is also interesting, as this allele lies in the TPR domain near the protein's interface with IFT121 (Figure 8E).
evidence: This statement describes the location of a disease variant in the structural model, shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The localization of the IFT139 L795P variant seems normal.
source: The localization of this variant seems normal (Davis et al., 2011), yet functional assays in both zebrafish and C. elegans demonstrate that the allele is pathogenic suggesting a biochemical perturbation (Davis et al., 2011; Niwa, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Davis et al., 2011 and Niwa, 2016.

claim: Functional assays in zebrafish and C. elegans demonstrate that the IFT139 L795P allele is pathogenic.
source: The localization of this variant seems normal (Davis et al., 2011), yet functional assays in both zebrafish and C. elegans demonstrate that the allele is pathogenic suggesting a biochemical perturbation (Davis et al., 2011; Niwa, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Davis et al., 2011 and Niwa, 2016.

claim: The IFT139 L795P allele's pathogenicity may be exerted by disrupting interaction with IFT121.
source: Our model suggests that this allele's pathogenicity may be exerted by disrupting interaction with IFT121 (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the location of the variant in the structural model, shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The combination of cross-linking mass-spectrometry, AlphaFold-Multimer, and integrative modeling produced a highly concordant structure with the single particle cryo-EM reconstruction.
source: The fact that the combination of cross-linking mass-spectrometry, AlphaFold-Multimer, and integrative modeling produced a highly concordant structure with the significantly higher resolution single particle cryo-EM reconstruction (Hesketh et al., 2022) also suggests that such a readily accessible combined modeling approach might be broadly suitable for many other protein complexes.
evidence: This statement compares the current study's approach to that of Hesketh et al., 2022.

claim: When IFT trains reach the ciliary tip, a structural rearrangement occurs where kinesin dissociates from the complex and dynein motors power the retrograde movement.
source: It has been previously observed that when the IFT trains (including IFT-A, IFT-B, and the BBsome) reach the ciliary tip, a structural rearrangement occurs where kinesin dissociates from the complex and the dynein motors power the retrograde movement (Chien et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Chien et al., 2017.

claim: The retrograde IFT arrangement differs in morphology from the anterograde arrangement.
source: The subtomogram average that we have used in our polymeric model represents the anterograde arrangement and while the retrograde arrangement is not known, it was shown to differ in morphology from the anterograde arrangement (Stepanek and Pigino, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Stepanek and Pigino, 2016.

claim: The assembly of the IFT-A complex into oligomeric trains suggests structural rearrangements relative to a monomeric IFT-A complex.
source: Similarly, the assembly of the IFT-A complex into oligomeric trains clearly suggests structural rearrangements relative to a monomeric IFT-A complex (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplement 1), consistent with observations for the human IFT-A monomer (Hesketh et al., 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hesketh et al., 2022 and shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Chemical cross-links were derived from the monomeric IFT-A assembly based on known size calibrants for SEC column chromatography.
source: Based on known size calibrants for our SEC column chromatography, our chemical cross-links were derived from the monomeric IFT-A assembly (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement describes the experimental approach and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Concentrating the IFT-A samples might have induced some degree of oligomerization and interactions with IFT-B.
source: However, as the samples were subsequently further concentrated for crosslinking, we speculate that concentrating the particles might have induced some degree of oligomerization and interactions with IFT-B, which may explain the small number of cross-links consistent with IFT-A/A and IFT-A/B interactions.
evidence: This is speculation by the authors about potential sample behavior.

claim: A large cross-link violation was observed between the WD40 domain of IFT121 (K16) and IFT144 (K831) in the monomeric integrative model.
source: For example, in our monomeric integrative model of the IFT-A complex, we observe a large cross-link violation between the WD40 domain of IFT121 (K16) and IFT144 (K831).
evidence: This statement describes a specific observation from the model.

claim: AlphaFold2 places the WD40 domains of IFT121 and IFT122 as interacting and is supported by low PAE values between the residues within this region.
source: Interestingly, while AlphaFold2 places the WD40 domains of IFT121 and IFT122 as interacting and is supported by low PAE values between the residues within this region, we observe no cross-links between the proteins in this region.
evidence: This statement describes a comparison between AlphaFold2 predictions and experimental cross-linking data.

claim: Cross-links are observed between the WD40 domains of IFT121 and IFT122 and other proteins.
source: We do, however, observe cross-links between the WD40 domains of IFT121 and IFT122 and other proteins.
evidence: This statement describes experimental cross-linking data.

claim: Cross-links between the WD40 domains of IFT121 and IFT122 and other proteins raise the possibility of domain rearrangements upon interactions with other proteins or transient rearrangements reflecting a dynamic and flexible complex.
source: These cross-links raise the possibility of domain rearrangements of the WD40 domains of IFT121 and IFT122 upon interactions with other proteins, or even transient rearrangements reflecting a dynamic and flexible complex.
evidence: This is speculation by the authors based on the cross-linking data.

claim: Additional local structural rearrangements are likely to occur with changes to assembly state and direction of travel.
source: As for any structural biology study, while certain regions of the model are highly confident, we anticipate that additional local structural rearrangements are likely to occur with changes to assembly state and direction of travel.
evidence: This is a general statement about the limitations of structural models.

claim: Tetrahymena thermophila SB715 were grown in Modified Neff medium.
source: Tetrahymena thermophila SB715 were obtained from the Tetrahymena Stock Center (Cornell University, Ithaca, NY) and grown in Modified Neff medium obtained from the stock center.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: Cilia were released from Tetrahymena by pH shock or dibucaine treatment.
source: Briefly, cilia were released by either pH shock or dibucaine treatment and recovered by centrifugation.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: Cilia were extracted with 1% NP40 in HEPES-Cilia Wash Buffer for cross-linking experiments.
source: For cross-linking experiments, cilia were extracted with 1% NP40 in HEPES-Cilia Wash Buffer (H-CWB, where 50 mM HEPES pH 7.4 was used in place of the 50 mM Tris to ensure compatibility with DSSO, and 0.1 mM PMSF was added.)
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used.

claim: IFT-A and B were estimated by mass spectrometry to each comprise approximately 3% of the sample after SEC fractionation.
source: For sample preparation, IFT-A containing fractions from two identical sequential separations were pooled; IFT-A and B were estimated by mass spectrometry to each comprise approximately 3% of the sample.
evidence: This describes the experimental sample composition.

claim: The final average cryo-ET structure was calculated from 9,350 particles derived from 96 tomograms.
source: The final average was calculated from 9,350 particles derived from 96 tomograms.
evidence: This describes the cryo-ET data collection.

claim: The resolution of the cryo-ET structure was estimated to 2.3 nm by Fourier shell correlation using a cut-off criterion of 0.5.
source: The resolution was estimated to 2.3 nm by Fourier shell correlation, using a cut-off criterion of 0.5.
evidence: This describes the resolution of the cryo-ET structure.
